\begin{center} {\Large \textbf{Chapter 3: Motion Reference Sheet}} \end{center} \hrule \vspace{0.15in} \textbf{\large Position, Velocity, and Acceleration} \textbf{Position} tells where an object is. \medskip \textbf{Velocity} tells how fast and in what direction position is changing. \[ \boxed{ v=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} =\frac{\text{change in position}}{\text{change in time}} } \] Velocity is the \textbf{slope of a position vs.\ time graph}. \begin{itemize} \setlength\itemsep{0pt} \item Positive velocity: motion in the positive direction \item Negative velocity: motion in the negative direction \item Zero velocity: the object is not moving \end{itemize} \textbf{Acceleration} tells how quickly velocity is changing. \[ \boxed{ a=\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =\frac{\text{change in velocity}}{\text{change in time}} } \] Acceleration is the \textbf{slope of a velocity vs.\ time graph}. \vspace{0.08in} \hrule \vspace{0.15in} \textbf{\large Slope} \[ \boxed{ \text{slope} = \frac{\text{vertical change}}{\text{horizontal change}} } \] \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c} \textbf{Graph} & \textbf{Slope represents} \\ \hline position vs.\ time & velocity \\ velocity vs.\ time & acceleration \end{tabular} \end{center} \vspace{0.08in} \hrule \vspace{0.15in} \textbf{\large Average Velocity} \[ \boxed{ v_{\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}} } \] Equivalently, \[ \boxed{ \text{displacement} = v_{\mathrm{avg}}\,\Delta t } \] \vspace{0.08in} \hrule \vspace{0.15in} \textbf{\large Relative Velocity and Vector Addition} When an object moves through moving water, air, or another moving medium, \textbf{add the velocity vectors}. \[ \boxed{ \vec v_{\mathrm{object/ground}} = \vec v_{\mathrm{object/medium}} + \vec v_{\mathrm{medium/ground}} } \] \begin{itemize} \setlength\itemsep{0pt} \item Vectors pointing in the \textbf{same direction} add. \item Vectors pointing in \textbf{opposite directions} subtract. \item For perpendicular vectors, draw a right triangle. \end{itemize} For a right triangle, \[ \boxed{a^2+b^2=c^2} \] \vspace{0.08in} \hrule \vspace{0.15in} \newpage \textbf{\large Units and Symbols} \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c|c|c} \textbf{Quantity} & \textbf{Symbol} & \textbf{Unit} \\ \hline position / displacement & $x,\ y,\ \Delta x$ & m \\ velocity & $v$ & m/s \\ acceleration & $a$ & $\mathrm{m/s^2}$ \end{tabular} \end{center} The symbol $\Delta$ means \textbf{change in}: \[ \Delta x=x_{\mathrm{final}}-x_{\mathrm{initial}} \qquad\qquad \Delta v=v_{\mathrm{final}}-v_{\mathrm{initial}} \] \vspace{0.08in} \hrule \vspace{0.12in} \begin{center} \textbf{Pay attention to signs and directions.} A negative velocity or acceleration does \textbf{not} automatically mean ``slowing down.'' \end{center}
